prompt:
You describe a graph or chart from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What is plotted against what: for each axis, the quantity, the unit and the range (first and last tick labels).
2. Each curve or series: its label or condition (temperature, voltage, mode, ...) and its overall trend in words.
3. Values printed in the figure as text (annotations, labelled points, legend values). Do not estimate values from where a curve sits; if a value is not printed, describe the trend in words instead.

Figure type: graph or chart
Section: 17. LR-FHSS (LR20xx) > 17.1 LR-FHSS Modulation
Caption: Figure 17-1: LR-FHSS Spectral Plot Example
Text inside the figure (read from this image by a specialised OCR model; use these spellings): : LR4 NSS Spectral Piot Example | PHY Headers | Payload Frames | Bandwidth | Frequency | Time
Text that mentions the figure: From a spectral perspective, the LR-FHSS packet is divided into multiple frames, each transmitted over pseudo-randomly distributed frequencies, with configurable spacing known as the "Grid" or step size. The total spectral occupancy of the LR-FHSS packet is determined by the Bandwidth parameter. For a visual representation of LR-FHSS modulation, refer to Figure 17-1: LR-FHSS Spectral Plot Example.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".
